summary: Round r1 (restricted network). The route-cost question (Kolkata/Haldia vs Visakhapatnam vs potential Bangladeshi ports) is pending: no time or cost values were retrieved. Leads located or reused: World Bank NIRTTP project document (corridor baselines), World Bank LPI, UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport, ICRIER study of Nepal's transit through India, Indian Embassy commerce brief on the Treaty of Transit, Nepal customs statistics, WTO TPR 2025 and ICIMOD on the 2026 northern-route flood. The session web-search budget ran out before leads for time-release studies, NITDB traffic data, the Treaty of Transit text and letters of exchange, and any Nepal-Bangladesh transit arrangement could be located; these are data gaps. A route matrix and reference-shipment method are specified.

findings.claim: Route comparison uses a standard 40ft/20ft container import from an East Asian transhipment hub to ICD Birgunj as the reference shipment; costs are expressed in USD current prices per TEU with the survey date recorded; time is median door-to-door days.

Bangladeshi ports are treated as 'potential' routes: they enter the scenario model only as an alternative-route option whose availability is a labelled scenario assumption until an operating arrangement is documented.

data_gaps: Treaty of Transit text, protocol and letters of exchange (Visakhapatnam, Dhamra, rail/inland waterways) not located as primary documents.
Nepal time-release studies (Department of Customs/WB) and NITDB ICD traffic statistics not located.
No document located on an operational Nepal-Bangladesh port transit arrangement (Mongla/Chattogram).
Freight-rate series (Drewry/SCFI) are licensed or not in catalog; UNCTAD RMT provides only indices.
Nepal-China Transit Transport Agreement protocol and northern route cost data not located.
The session web-search budget was exhausted part-way through r1; further leads for this task must be located in r2 or by the orchestrator.

assumptions.text: Route comparison uses a standard 40ft/20ft container import from an East Asian transhipment hub to ICD Birgunj as the reference shipment; costs are expressed in USD current prices per TEU with the survey date recorded; time is median door-to-door days.

Bangladeshi ports are treated as 'potential' routes: they enter the scenario model only as an alternative-route option whose availability is a labelled scenario assumption until an operating arrangement is documented.

challenges.text: EXP-04 proxy (third-country imports through southern customs offices) cannot distinguish Kolkata/Haldia from Visakhapatnam; recommend adding NITDB ICD-by-port data as primary table and treating Bangladeshi routes as a separate optional-route exposure.
Chokepoint and cargo-insurance shocks (X31) should be passed as ocean-leg cost multipliers so that 21B's route matrix can apply them per route rather than as a single transit-cost shock.
Source catalog id nitdb exists but no endpoint lead has been located; suggest the orchestrator allocate search budget for NITDB, customs time-release studies and treaty texts in r2.

uncertainty: High. No time or cost value retrieved. LPI is perception-survey based and not route-specific; time-release studies are point-in-time; freight rates are volatile (post-2021 and Red Sea-related swings), so any route comparison must carry its survey date. Bangladeshi-route viability depends on arrangements not yet documented.

route_cost_comparison.method: Build a route matrix; for each route record legal status, operational status, time components and cost components from primary sources (time-release studies, NIRTTP, NITDB, LPI KPIs, UNCTAD RMT freight indices). Keep survey-based (LPI) and transaction-based (time-release) measures separate and document differences. Convert calendar-year international data to Nepal FY only where it enters the model.
